public_source.title: Scheduled tasks in ChatGPT
observations: ChatGPT Scheduled supports one-time and recurring tasks and monitoring tasks.
Monitoring tasks can remember previous runs.
Scheduled tasks can use supported connected apps, including GitHub, when available for the account or workspace.
Active-task limits vary by plan; exact hourly schedules require an eligible paid plan.
Connected-app actions can depend on granted permissions and may require approval; inactive tasks may pause automatically.

tested_scope: Public-documentation sufficiency probe only for the narrow useful-outcome-parity proposition that recurring scheduled Chat plus available GitHub transport can independently establish durable, unattended, conflict-safe checkpoint persistence/reconstruction equivalent to the current candidate's material outcome. No new checker execution, no scheduler inspection, no other-role semantics, and no broader route acceptance were tested.

supports: Recurring Chat execution is a documented native capability.
GitHub app use from Scheduled is documented when available.
does_not_establish: Exact GitHub Contents create/update/readback semantics for this candidate solely from Scheduled documentation.
Unattended execution with zero approval dependency for every required write.
Duplicate/conflict safety or idempotency for repeated writes.
Zero incremental monetary cost or plan-independence for exact hourly scheduling.
Absence of every finite plan/quota dependency.
finding.reasoning: The source establishes recurring execution and broad GitHub-app availability, but the candidate hard gate requires the useful material outcome itself to be demonstrated under exact route constraints. Conditional app availability, possible approval requirements, plan-dependent active-task limits/exact-hourly availability, and lack of source-level proof for exact durable Contents write/readback semantics prevent promotion of useful_outcome_parity to true.
